title: Track Lake integrity incidents, investigations, and repeat-failure alerts
body:
## Purpose

Record investigations of suspected Lake artifact/reuse failures and integrity-guard incidents. Part of #222; that issue continues to own the stronger reuse contract and replacement work. Keep this tracker open across individual incident recoveries while the underlying problem remains unresolved. This is temporary investigation guidance, not a permanent reporting duty.

Normal cold-build invalidations (outputs/traces have never been built) are not incidents. Record unexpected output mismatches, recurring missing/malformed evidence in previously built modules, post-build integrity rejection, and suspected stale-artifact failures from direct Lake/editor use. Ordinary source errors are not Lake bugs without supporting evidence.

## Before investigating

Read this issue and its comments for an existing investigation matching the module, diagnostics, artifact/trace identities, and circumstances. Collect evidence from each unexpected occurrence and compare it with earlier records. A previous investigation is a comparison point, not a reason to stop investigating. Similar error wording alone does not establish the same cause.

The aim is evidence across multiple occurrences unless the investigation establishes a clear result. State exactly which question that result answers and its limits before narrowing further investigation. Separate the reuse mechanism, the creation of inconsistent artifacts, and their propagation. An established result for one does not settle the others. Reuse a demonstrated reproduction or recovery procedure without rerunning it needlessly, but still capture the new occurrence's available identities, provenance and outcome. Repeat alerts supplement this evidence gathering; they do not replace it.

**If the failure has already been investigated, alert the owner in the current conversation**, even if automatic recovery succeeds. State the affected task, what matched the prior investigation, what remains uncertain, and whether recovery/validation passed. Link the prior investigation and append an occurrence record here, including evidence relevant to the remaining open questions. A comment or GitHub mention alone does not establish that the owner was alerted.

For sub-agents: report the recurrence promptly to the parent/coordinating agent, with those details and the issue/comment link. The top-level agent relays the alert to the owner in the active conversation and includes it in its final report. The coordinator owns one incident comment; sub-agents supply evidence rather than posting duplicate comments. If tracker access is unavailable, return a prepared comment and disclose that it was not posted. Alerting does not require pausing safe investigation or automatic recovery for approval.

## Investigation record

Use one comment per incident, updating it as results arrive:

- UTC time, task/PR, candidate commit, Lean/Lake versions, command and exit status.
- Affected modules and the exact relevant diagnostic; distinguish guard-triggered recovery from verification failure.
- Prior investigation link and classification: known recurrence, suspected new mechanism, or unresolved. Explain the evidence for the classification.
- Available source/trace/output identities and provenance clues; note concurrent writers or copied caches. Mark evidence lost to automatic invalidation as unavailable, not reconstructed fact.
- Probes, recovery actions, and outcomes. State whether source changes were needed and whether guarded incremental validation and any fresh validation passed separately.
- Remaining uncertainty and owner-alert status (delivered by the top-level agent, or pending relay).

Preserve relevant logs and surviving artifacts locally before further manual cleanup. Redact secrets and machine-specific details from public comments; publish concise diagnostics and hashes, not raw session logs or binaries. Follow the repository's `docs/agents/lake-integrity-incidents.md` recovery runbook. A fresh-build success bypasses project artifacts; it does not repair the incremental cache or prove the guard correct.

## Already investigated: inherited GraphEmission artifact

Upstream reuse report: https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/issues/16123

Earlier evidence: #222, especially https://github.com/VladimirMarko/conaled/issues/222#issuecomment-6530717664 and https://github.com/VladimirMarko/conaled/issues/222#issuecomment-6531042331.

The session review found the GraphEmission failure in #185, #240, #242, #249, #259, #252, #256 and #268 after the incremental-acceptance policy change. These are task encounters, not eight established Lake bugs. Preserved binaries from #185/#240/#242/#249/#252/#256 match the known #268 artifact byte-for-byte. #259 has matching symptoms and metadata but no separately confirmed binary identity.

Known binary: `SquareKit.Internal.GraphEmission.olean`, 1,652,536 bytes, SHA-256 `1706bc30e261488c78ece61d611928de6a4262f329ae4df4d5ea15b1ef2fdc0a`. The characteristic diagnostic includes unknown `GraphEmissionPure.ArtifactTyped`. The trace's output identity was `8e3cc7e2fd7486e2.olean`, while the adjacent sidecar contained `83a9a9a995929b8b`.

The evidence supports repeated propagation of one inconsistent artifact. The operation that originally mixed outputs and metadata remains unknown, so investigation of artifact creation and propagation remains open. Further occurrences should capture donor/copy history, trace and output identities, and available writer/timing evidence rather than treating this origin question as resolved. No second Lake failure mechanism was established by the session-log search. The portable reproduction deliberately constructs inconsistent outputs; it does not show Lake spontaneously creating them.

Repository evidence: `docs/research/lake-session-failure-review.md` and `docs/research/lake-output-cache-mismatch.md`, recorded with the guard in local commit `1d64ccecdaeb8e37706e7cee068e5cb3ecd8740e` (not yet pushed when this issue was opened). The full portable reproduction is available in the upstream report.


## Retirement and closure

Once the underlying problem is fixed or otherwise handled, record the resolution, supporting evidence and any remaining limits. A single successful recovery is not by itself that resolution; an explicitly accepted mitigation or disposition can be sufficient without proving the original cause.

Close this tracker as part of retiring its active instructions:

- [ ] Record the fix or accepted disposition and why further incident watching is no longer needed.
- [ ] Remove the temporary incident trigger from `AGENTS.md` and the active tracking/alert instructions from `README.md`.
- [ ] Remove the temporary runbook at `docs/agents/lake-integrity-incidents.md`, or retain only recovery guidance still needed by the implemented tooling and remove its incident-watching/reporting duties.
- [ ] Update incoming links and remove any other active pointers to this temporary workflow. Retain historical research notes and issue records, marking their investigation status resolved or otherwise handled.
- [ ] Review and validate those documentation changes, then close this issue. Retain ordinary `check.sh` acceptance requirements and any still-needed guard documentation.

An agent encountering a closed tracker should check its resolution, not continue the retired reporting workflow. If active pointers remain, report that cleanup omission to its coordinator and remove them through the normal documentation workflow.
